_doc: Chức Hà Các lineage (rules-proposals R5). Re-ordered Fire, Wood -> Wood, Fire to its seat (place 1013: Wood 25.05 %, Fire 16.7 %; passes by a hair). Outer gate: mulberry-leaf-breath (Wood + Fire, proposal). Inner gate and above: unbroken-thread-canon (Wood, proposal). Secret art: fire-in-the-thread (inner, Fire, proposal). Proposals are unpriced.

lineage.tree_route_note: The unbroken thread: Creeping Vine and Binding Vine to bind and slow, then Wutong Perch so the Fire that runs along the thread burns longer.

techniques.name: Mulberry Leaf Breath (Tang Diệp Tức)
techniques.concept: The weavers' first method, breathed in the worm sheds among the trays of mulberry leaves, where the air is warm and green. Wood qi is drawn in as the worms draw in the leaf, and a little warmth is kept in the belly as the sheds keep it for the worms. It makes patient, steady hands.

arts.concept: Throws a fine thread that clings to a foe: a light Wood hit that slows them slightly for a few seconds.
A small heal over time on the holder and adjacent allies.

techniques.lore: The silk families of Tang Điền have breathed this way in the worm sheds since the mulberry fields were planted (A300). Thân Vân Cẩm wrote it down in 1150.

techniques.name: Unbroken Thread Canon (Bất Đoạn Ti Kinh)
techniques.concept: A reeler's method. The cultivator draws her qi out as one thread that must never break, the way a reeler draws a cocoon's single filament; each layer is a longer, stronger thread. In a fight she spins threads that bind, cut and carry her arts along them, and a foe caught in several threads is pulled and slowed. If her thread breaks, her qi recoils.

arts.concept: Binds a foe with a thread: they are slowed and pulled a step toward the holder; a second bind roots them for a second.
Weaves a net of threads in front of the holder for a few seconds: blows through it lose force, and foes inside gain Wood stacks.

A passive art. Your thread on the foe (a Reel In bind) breaks when the foe fires a `heavy` or `slow` art or is Displaced by anything but your own pulls; when it breaks you lose 4 % of your maximum linh lực (the recoil). A thread that runs its whole time unbroken ties a Knot (a self-counter, no cap, kept for the fight): each Knot makes your thread arts lay one more Wood stack, and Burning Thread lay 2 more Burn stacks.

techniques.lore: The reelers of Hỏa Ti Trấn cultivated by this method before the town burned in 590 (V165); its survivors carried it to Tang Điền's sheds. It has no Fire in it: the fire was always the vent's.

techniques.name: Fire in the Thread (Hỏa Chức Quyết)
techniques.concept: Thân Vân Cẩm's art: putting fire into silk with the weaver's own Fire rather than the vent's. The weaver runs her Fire along the thread as she weaves, layer by layer, so the cloth holds it. Silk made this way burns without burning and wards against fire, but holds the heat only a season before it chars. In a fight the holder's threads catch fire along their length.

arts.concept: Sets her threads alight: each foe bound by a thread takes Fire damage over time and gains Fire stacks.
Out of combat, a craft: weaves fire-silk cloth that wards against Fire; it decays after a season.

techniques.lore: Made by Thân Vân Cẩm between 1148 and 1150, after her mother Hầu Tố Cẩm burned her hands trying the same thing without a method. It is why the pavilion exists (V172).
